bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USDM has canonical collateral/order issuance on Ethereum and a peripheral MegaETH LayerZero direct OFT representation. The route uses burn/debit on the source and mint/credit on the paired destination; it is not an external lock/mint route. The common 4-of-8 Safe controls both OFT proxies' bridge mint/burn, upgrades, peers, administration, and rate limits, while token-level arbitrary mint authority remains separately assessed under native Ethereum Mint Authority.

routeChecks.rateLimits: The verified implementation exposes owner-configured per-destination-EID rate limits and rejects unconfigured destinations. The current limit and window values were not independently decoded in this pass, so no favorable numeric bound is asserted.

controls.capDescription: The common Safe controls bridge burn/debit and mint/credit administration, UUPS upgrades, peer/delegate configuration, and destination-EID rate limits for the direct Ethereum-MegaETH OFT route. The route's ordinary burn/mint accounting is supply-conserving, but an owner-authorized implementation change or token-level arbitrary mint remains an adverse failure surface; that token-level mint authority is separately scored under native Ethereum Mint Authority.
bypassSurfaces: LayerZero Endpoint V2, ULN, DVN, Executor, and delegate governance are external/common failure domains; current USDm-specific values were not independently replayed.
The common Safe can replace either OFT implementation or change peers and rate limits without an on-chain timelock.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770580 and MegaETH block 24121857 (2026-08-16), the verified xUSDOFTUpgradeable proxies used reciprocal LayerZero Endpoint V2 peers: Ethereum EID 30398 pointed to the MegaETH token and MegaETH EID 30101 pointed to the Ethereum token, with MegaETH isPeer(...) true. LayerZero's direct OFT pattern debits or burns on the source and credits or mints on the paired destination, so the reviewed route is external-validated burn/mint and supply-conserving at the route level, not lock/mint. The common Safe 0x141c03abc062a9d5d4238e1666b849c929e53cb2 was 4-of-8 at Ethereum block 25770585 with eight current owners and no enabled modules; direct guard and fallback reads reverted. The Safe owns both UUPS proxies and can upgrade implementations, change peers/delegates and rate limits, and manage minters without a timelock. Current LayerZero DVN, Executor, delegate, enforced-options, and USDm-specific rate-limit values were not independently replayed. The implementation's arbitrary token mint function remains native Ethereum mint-authority evidence and is not erased by the route's conserved OFT accounting.
